title: How a Motorcycle Responds to Your Controls

slides.title: The Control Loop
slides.objective: Give the listener a mental map from rider input to motorcycle response and feedback.
slides.headline: Every control changes the motorcycle through forces, torque, and available grip.
slides.visual_description: A clockwise loop connects rider inputs to drivetrain and brakes, then tyre-road forces, motorcycle response, and rider feedback.

beats.summary: Motorcycle controls work as one connected system rather than as isolated switches.
beats.narration_guidance: Introduce the control loop from the rider's perspective without listing detailed physics.

beats.summary: The throttle and clutch together shape how engine torque reaches the motorcycle.
beats.narration_guidance: Describe torque delivery conceptually and avoid implying that either control acts alone.

beats.summary: The selected gear changes the relationship between engine speed and wheel speed.
beats.narration_guidance: Set up gear ratio as a relationship, not as an exact calculation.

beats.summary: Brakes reduce wheel speed, but tyre-road grip limits the force the motorcycle can use.
beats.narration_guidance: End the overview with grip as the common constraint on acceleration and braking.

deep_dive.explanation: A rider applies a control, observes the motorcycle's response through motion and feel, and adjusts the next input. Throttle, clutch, gears, brakes, and steering therefore form a connected feedback loop.
caveats: Available tyre grip constrains every force transmitted at the road.

deep_dive.explanation: Progressive inputs make changes in tyre force and chassis load easier to manage than abrupt inputs.
caveats: This is a conceptual explanation, not riding instruction for every situation.

slides.title: Clutch and Gear System
slides.objective: Explain why the drivetrain needs a clutch and multiple gear ratios.
slides.headline: The clutch controls connection; the gearbox selects the ratio.
slides.visual_description: A left-to-right drivetrain path highlights the clutch connection and a selectable gearbox ratio before the rear wheel.

beats.summary: The clutch connects or disconnects engine torque from the gearbox.
beats.narration_guidance: Explain the clutch as a controllable connection rather than an on-off mystery.

beats.summary: In the friction zone, the clutch transfers only part of the available torque.
beats.narration_guidance: Describe partial engagement and controlled torque transfer in plain language.

beats.summary: Reducing drivetrain load helps the gearbox move from one ratio to another.
beats.narration_guidance: Keep the explanation conceptual and avoid prescribing a shifting technique.

beats.summary: Smooth clutch re-engagement restores drive without a sharp change at the rear wheel.
beats.narration_guidance: Connect smooth engagement to avoiding a jerk without making a universal riding claim.

deep_dive.explanation: The clutch provides a controllable connection between the rotating engine and gearbox so the motorcycle can start, stop, and change ratios without forcing both sides to match instantly.
caveats: Clutch design and operation vary by motorcycle.

deep_dive.explanation: Many motorcycles use several friction plates running in oil to package useful torque capacity into a compact assembly.
caveats: The presentation does not assume every motorcycle uses this design.

deep_dive.explanation: A rapid connection can impose a sudden speed mismatch on the drivetrain, which the rider may feel as a jerk or which may stall the engine at low speed.
caveats: The exact response depends on speed, gear, throttle, and motorcycle design.

slides.title: How Power Reaches the Wheel
slides.objective: Explain the drivetrain as a sequence of torque and speed transformations.
slides.headline: Power follows a path from combustion to the rear tyre.
slides.visual_description: A staged flow traces torque from the engine through clutch, gearbox, chain-belt-or-shaft final drive, and rear wheel.

beats.summary: Combustion creates torque at the engine crankshaft.
beats.narration_guidance: Start the drivetrain path without expanding into combustion engineering.

beats.summary: The clutch controls whether that engine torque reaches the gearbox.
beats.narration_guidance: Connect this beat to the previous clutch slide without repeating its full explanation.

beats.summary: The selected gear trades wheel speed for mechanical advantage.
beats.narration_guidance: Explain why low gears feel stronger without claiming that gears create energy.

beats.summary: The final drive carries rotation from the gearbox output to the rear wheel.
beats.narration_guidance: Name chain, belt, and shaft as alternatives and finish at the tyre-road contact.

deep_dive.explanation: A lower gear produces more wheel torque for a given engine torque but requires more engine revolutions for the same wheel speed. A higher gear does the reverse.
caveats: Real losses mean the drivetrain is not perfectly efficient.

deep_dive.explanation: Gearbox and final-drive ratios determine how many engine revolutions correspond to one rear-wheel revolution.
caveats: Exact ratios differ across motorcycles and selected gears.

deep_dive.explanation: Motorcycles commonly transfer gearbox output through a chain, belt, or shaft before it reaches the rear wheel.
caveats: Each layout has different maintenance and packaging tradeoffs.

slides.title: Engine Braking
slides.objective: Explain why closing the throttle can slow the motorcycle without applying the wheel brakes.
slides.headline: A closed throttle lets drivetrain resistance slow the rear wheel.
slides.visual_description: The drivetrain arrows reverse direction from the moving rear wheel toward a resisting engine after the throttle closes.

beats.summary: Closing the throttle sharply reduces the engine's driving torque.
beats.narration_guidance: Distinguish reduced driving torque from applying the wheel brakes.

beats.summary: The moving motorcycle then keeps the engine turning through the drivetrain path.
beats.narration_guidance: Say that the wheel drives the engine through the drivetrain, not that the engine reverses direction.

beats.summary: Pumping and internal engine losses resist that motion.
beats.narration_guidance: Name the resistance sources briefly without presenting a detailed thermodynamic model.

beats.summary: A lower gear makes the engine turn faster at the same road speed, so the resisting effect feels stronger.
beats.narration_guidance: Connect the stronger sensation to gear ratio and retain the traction caveat.

deep_dive.explanation: At the same road speed, a lower gear requires a higher engine speed. With the throttle closed, that ratio couples more engine resistance back to the rear wheel, so the motorcycle slows more strongly.
caveats: Available tyre grip still limits deceleration.
An abrupt downshift can unsettle the rear wheel.

deep_dive.explanation: Wheel brakes create friction at the brake discs or drums, while engine braking comes from the drivetrain forcing a closed-throttle engine to keep turning.
caveats: Engine braking mainly acts through the driven wheel.

slides.title: Rev Matching During Downshifts
slides.objective: Explain rev matching as synchronizing engine speed with the lower gear's requirement.
slides.headline: A throttle blip reduces the speed mismatch during a downshift.
slides.visual_description: Two speed traces converge as a throttle blip raises engine speed toward the lower gear's target before clutch re-engagement.

beats.summary: At the same road speed, a lower gear requires the engine to turn faster.
beats.narration_guidance: Frame the target as a relationship rather than an exact RPM value.

beats.summary: Without matching, the rear wheel must accelerate the engine when the clutch reconnects.
beats.narration_guidance: Explain the source of the disturbance without calling every unmatched shift unsafe.

beats.summary: A controlled throttle blip raises engine speed closer to the lower gear's target.
beats.narration_guidance: State the purpose of the blip without giving prescriptive throttle amounts.

beats.summary: Smooth clutch release still matters; rev matching does not replace basic control.
beats.narration_guidance: Close with the limitation and avoid presenting an advanced technique as mandatory.

deep_dive.explanation: Rev matching raises engine speed toward the speed demanded by a lower gear at the current road speed, reducing the correction imposed when the clutch reconnects.
caveats: It does not replace a controlled clutch release.
Learners should prioritize safe and smooth control over aggressive technique.

deep_dive.explanation: A smaller engine-to-wheel speed mismatch can reduce the sudden drivetrain torque that disturbs the motorcycle during a downshift.
caveats: Road, traction, and motorcycle conditions still matter.

slides.title: Braking and ABS
slides.objective: Explain how braking uses tyre grip and how ABS responds near wheel lock.
slides.headline: Brakes create tyre force; ABS manages pressure near lock.
slides.visual_description: A braking-force path runs from lever pressure to the tyre-road contact, with a separate wheel-sensor feedback loop modulating pressure.

beats.summary: Brake controls create pressure in the braking system.
beats.narration_guidance: Explain the control-to-pressure path without specifying hardware dimensions or values.

beats.summary: The tyres turn braking force into deceleration at the road.
beats.narration_guidance: Keep tyre-road grip as the limiting boundary.

beats.summary: Weight transfer changes how much each wheel can contribute during deceleration.
beats.narration_guidance: Mention the changing wheel contributions without prescribing exact brake balance.

beats.summary: ABS detects excessive wheel slip and modulates pressure when lock is imminent.
beats.narration_guidance: State clearly that ABS manages available grip rather than creating more grip.

deep_dive.explanation: ABS uses wheel behavior to reduce and reapply brake pressure near lock, helping preserve rotation and steering ability within the grip that is available.
caveats: Surface and tyre conditions still affect stopping performance.

deep_dive.explanation: Deceleration transfers load toward the front tyre, which often lets the front brake contribute more while reducing the rear tyre's available contribution.
caveats: The exact balance varies with motorcycle, surface, load, and rider input.

deep_dive.explanation: A locked wheel no longer rolls with road speed, while controlled slip retains some rotation as the tyre generates braking force.
caveats: This presentation does not prescribe threshold-braking technique.
